items.description: An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26. Someone with that key could build counterfeit devices that pass the online check owners use to verify a Keystone. items.title: Critical HashiCorp Consul Kubernetes Flaw Allows Attackers to Gain Elevated Privileges
items.description: HashiCorp has released fixes for a Consul-k8s authorization bypass that could allow an attacker to gain elevated Consul privileges from another Kubernetes namespace. Tracked as CVE-2026-110720, the flaw affects deployments using automated system access control list management. HashiCorp disclosed the issue on October 26, 2026, and identified Consul-k8s 2.1.0 and 1.8.18 as patched releases. The…

items.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
items.description: Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations. Some fake login pages go beyond stealing passwords.
